title: task create allocates the next id from the current branch's .quest/tasks/ only, risking duplicate ids across unmerged branches
description:
Reported by lore-cli, reproduced there tonight (2026-09-13): quest task create run from dev allocated LCLI-476, an id already in use by a record sitting on an unmerged PR (#12, ids 476-479). Nothing warned; caught before commit by chance and refiled as LCLI-481. Root cause: the id allocator only reads the current working tree's .quest/tasks/, and .quest/ is committed per-branch like any other tracked directory, so any repo with an in-flight task branch can mint a duplicate id just by creating a task from a different ref (most commonly dev). The collision is silent at creation and surfaces later as a merge conflict, or worse as two records claiming one id in different histories that both look internally valid. Same family as id reuse after a tree reset: the allocator's notion of next is only as complete as the tree in front of it -- one case frees an id by discarding an uncommitted file, this one hides an id on another ref.

THIS TASK'S OWN ID WAS RESERVED BY HAND (--id QCLI-279) BECAUSE THE BUG REPRODUCED WHILE FILING IT. Letting quest task create auto-allocate from this branch (cut fresh from origin/dev) handed back QCLI-278 -- already committed and pushed on a sibling branch (docs/QCLI-278-runbook-provenance-note, PR #42) for an entirely unrelated task. Caught before commit by manually scanning commit c195ba0206909fe25e2828e75c1ba7a24ff61fb9

    chore(QCLI-269): file two tracker defects found by opum-marketplace (#21)
    
    Both reported by opum-marketplace while closing OMARK-42, both reproduced
    here against quest 0.6.0 in a scratch workspace before filing.
    
    QCLI-269 -- `--check-ac N` is 1-based while `task view` renders a 0-based
    `index` on both `--json` and `--plain`, so a caller who passes back the
    number the record showed them checks the preceding criterion and gets
    exit 0 with a full task record. Two corrections to the report are carried
    in the task: out-of-range N is already rejected (exit 2 below 1, exit 6
    above the length), so the silent failure is confined to an in-range wrong
    N -- and `quest instructions task-creation` points callers at a 1-based
    numbered list that `task view` does not print, so the documented
    mitigation does not exist.
    
    QCLI-270 -- `task complete` rejects `--final-summary`, and the rejection
    says "requires a reference and an explicit actor" when both were supplied
    and the unknown flag is the actual cause. The misleading diagnostic was
    not in the report and is the sharper half.
    
    Tracker-only; no code change. `lore check` exits 0.

    QCLI-267: document the v0.6.0 tag's provenance, and gate the next release on it (#13)
    
    * QCLI-267: record the v0.6.0 tag provenance problem and its options
    
    No tag created, moved or deleted. The task records measured facts -- the tag
    peels to the post-recreation initial commit, npm's gitHead for 0.6.0 points
    at a commit GitHub returns 422 for -- five options, one ruled out on
    evidence, and what each consumer would need to know.
    
    Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>
    Claude-Session: https://claude.ai/code/session_01LwG5hMgRdijde3DH6Hv6KG
    
    * QCLI-267: gate releases on provenance the repository can still show
    
    A published version's provenance must be something this repository can still
    show you. @opum-ai/quest 0.6.0 records gitHead=ce551cf4; the repository was
    deleted and recreated on 2026-09-10; ce551cf4 no longer exists anywhere and
    GitHub returns 422 for it. The v0.6.0 tag meanwhile peels to the
    post-recreation initial commit. Two public claims about one artifact, neither
    matching the other, and nothing anywhere noticed -- a downstream site found
    it by getting a 404 on a link it served in production.
    
    User decision recorded on the task: document it, fix it forward. No tag was
    moved or deleted; that stays in the irreversible set.
    
    Documented: a GitHub Release now exists for v0.6.0 stating the provenance
    plainly, including that npm carries no attestations so gitHead is the only
    provenance it has, and that the immutable npm version is the better thing to
    cite than these tags.
    
    Gated: scripts/qualification/release-provenance.mjs, wired into the release
    workflow. --pre asserts the tag matches package.json, the commit exists, and
    it is an ancestor of origin/main. --post asserts the registry's gitHead for
    what was just published is the commit it was released from -- the only moment
    both halves exist and can be compared.
    
    Negative-tested, including against the live registry: --post reproduces this
    exact defect today, reporting that 0.6.0 records ce551cf4 but was released
    from ef9d33a. The check catches what it was written for rather than being
    assumed to.

    Initial commit: fresh history after repository deletion/recreation (OPAG-70)
    
    Replaces the previous quest-cli history in full. The prior repository was
    deleted and recreated -- not merely branch-replaced -- because GitHub
    retains a refs/pull/<N>/head ref for every pull request a repository has
    ever had (358 of them here), those refs belong to the repository rather
    than to any branch, and no repository-admin action removes them. A
    branch-replacement-only rewrite, verified against a sibling repository
    that had already done exactly that, left the complete original content
    fully fetchable on request regardless of what happened to dev/main/tags.
    Deletion and recreation is the only mechanism that actually removes them.
    
    This commit is the cleaned working tree as of 2026-09-10: current source,
    tests, docs, and tracker state, with retired/fleet-internal content
    already removed in two prior passes (OPAG-70's CLAUDE.md strip, and a
    separate cleanup of a stale archive/handovers/ directory carrying
    pre-Quest Backlog.md-campaign coordination notes). The complete prior
    history, including every commit and every PR, is preserved offline and
    privately at /Volumes/external/archive/quest-cli/history-2026-09-10/
    (verified restorable via fsck and a full commit walk immediately before
    this repository was deleted) -- it does not return to GitHub.
    
    Accepted, knowingly: all 9 prior git tags are gone from this repository
    (preserved in the archive); @opum-ai/quest@0.6.0's published npm SLSA
    provenance attestation binds a commit that no longer exists here; there is
    no old-to-new commit correspondence, because a fresh init has none to
    carry. Authorized directly by this session's own user, distinct from and
    in addition to the two force-pushes authorized earlier in this same
    campaign before the branch-replacement approach was found insufficient
    and abandoned in favor of this.
    
    Co-Authored-By: Claude Sonnet 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

This session separately hit the divergent-content half of the same hazard resolving a cherry-pick conflict on .quest/tasks/QCLI-271.json between chore/QCLI-271-release-0.6.2 and dev (resolved correctly, no data lost, but it demonstrates the failure mode is not only duplicate ids at creation -- it is also divergent content for one id across refs, merging as a text conflict in a file no human wrote).

Fix shapes suggested by opum-agent, none chosen yet: (a) consult all refs when allocating (git log --all --diff-filter=A --name-only -- .quest/tasks/ enumerates every id ever created on any branch); (b) refuse to allocate when the working tree is not the branch carrying the newest records; (c) allocate, then warn loudly if the id exists on any other ref. (c) is the cheapest and catches it at the only moment it is still free to fix, but reading all refs on every create has a real cost against quest's own design goal of working on a plain directory -- weigh a warning that fires only when another ref actually contains a colliding id, which would get the safety without paying the cost on every create.

acceptanceCriteria.text: A decision is made and recorded among the suggested fix shapes (refs-aware allocation, refuse-if-stale-tree, or allocate-then-warn) or an explicit reason none is warranted

If implemented, quest task create run on a branch missing a newer id that exists on another local ref either refuses, warns, or allocates a non-colliding id -- demonstrated with a reproduction of this task's own filing (QCLI-278 already existed on a sibling unmerged branch when this task was created from a branch that could not see it)
The chosen behavior is documented in quest instructions task-creation so an agent understands the guarantee before relying on it
